schemeScope: Combined Ordinary scheme. PDF 12–13 Léamhthuiscint A (with the Paper 2 heading; its language deduction and penalty note at the end of 13); 14–15 Léamhthuiscint B (its language deduction and penalty note on 16); 17 Prós Ainmnithe (2A); 18 Prós Roghnach (2B); 19–21 Filíocht Ainmnithe (3A, its language deduction and the examiner’s note on 21); 22–23 Filíocht Roghnach (3B); 24 modified marking (SMM, no bands). PDF 1–11 belong to Paper 1; 25–27 are blank and 28 empty.
reviewMethod: Every paper page (1–3 cover and instructions, 4–7 the two reading passages, 8–12 literature) and every applicable scheme page read in the text layer and checked against the printed page (the literature pages 8–12 rendered); the scheme’s bullets are SymbolMT glyphs, read with their font; each prompt and scheme slice is asserted against the PDFs by the builder.

nonPoolDecisions: Reading: all ten questions are required; each printed (a)/(b) part is a 5-mark practice card beside the whole question. Two-point items (“3 mharc + 2 mharc”, “An chéad … = 3 mharc; an dara … = 2 mharc”) are order-dependent (first correct point 3, second 2) and stay whole at 0/3/5; single answers allow 0/5, or 0/3/5 where the scheme prints a 3-mark partial answer.
Reading language: “Gaeilge lochtach: 0 - 5 a bhaint den iomlán a gnóthaíodh.” is one deduction from each 50-mark passage total; cards state it without applying it inside a part.

Prescribed prose (2A): (a) Hurlamaboc asks for a summary covering five printed points (“Luaigh na pointí seo: (i) … (v)”) and the scheme prices it “5 phointe eolais agus 5 mharc ar gach pointe eolais. (5 mharc = 2 mharc ar lomphointe eolais agus 3 mharc ar fhorbairt.)”: the whole question is a 25-mark card with each printed point its own 5-mark criterion, and every point is also a practice card. (b) Oisín i dTír na nÓg is a 25-mark card (five points at 2 + 3); 2014 prints no film or play in 2A.

Prescribed poetry (3A): each poem is a whole 25-mark card with its printed tariffs ((a) Géibheann: (i) 8, (ii) 8, (iii) 9; (b) Colscaradh: (i) 8, (ii) 8, (iii) 9) and one 0–4 Gaeilge deduction; every printed sub-question is also a practice card. 3A(a)(i) prints four questions (a)–(d) at 2 each: each question is also its own practice card.

Optional prose (2B) and optional poetry (3B) stay whole: the text is open content chosen by the candidate. 2B(a) is a novel extract (protagonist 1, five points 22, title and author 2); 2B(b) a folk tale (five points 23, title 2); 2014 prints no optional film or play. 3B(a) asks for a modern poem by a woman and 3B(b) a modern poem by a man.
Choice is not a route: Ceist 2 and Ceist 3 are each A or B; each printed question is one card carrying the printed choice and “Freagair (a) agus (b) anseo.”; no combination cards.
Literature language: “[Gaeilge lochtach: 0 – 4 a bhaint den iomlán a gnóthaíodh.]” is one deduction from each 25-mark question, never inside one sub-question.
sourceFindings: Paper 2 = 200: Ceist 1 reading 100 (A Sibéal Davitt – Rinceoir ar an Sean-Nós 50, B Brian Ó Drisceoil - Laoch Mór Rugbaí 50; ten questions at (a) 5 + (b) 5 each), Ceist 2 prose 50 (A Prós Ainmnithe: (a) Hurlamaboc 25 + (b) Oisín i dTír na nÓg 25; or B Prós Roghnach: (a) giota as úrscéal 25 + (b) scéal béaloidis 25), Ceist 3 poetry 50 (A Filíocht Ainmnithe: (a) Géibheann 25 + (b) Colscaradh 25; or B Filíocht Roghnach: (a) a modern poem by a woman 25 + (b) a modern poem by a man 25).

The scheme draws its bullets with the SymbolMT glyph “x” (PDF 12–15); Calibri draws one space inside text as glyph 3, which the text layer returns as U+0003 (PDF 13 “Isi nGaeltacht Chonamara”, printed “Is i nGaeltacht Chonamara”). The builder reads each span with its font, maps only the reviewed SymbolMT glyph, and reads glyph 3 as a space.

The scheme’s text layer stores ten boxed headings with the page body (“Páipéar II (200 marc)”, “CEIST 1 (A + B) - LÉAMHTHUISCINT - 100 marc”, “A (50 marc)”, “B (50 marc)”, the CEIST 2/3 and section boxes); the builder removes those exact strings (count pinned).

2014 prints no note above the reading questions; each part prints its own split (“3 mharc + 2 mharc”, “An chéad scoil atá cruinn = 3 mharc; an dara scoil luaite agus cruinn = 2 mharc”). Each passage closes with “[Gaeilge lochtach: 0 - 5 …]” and the penalty note (“Nóta: Gearrfar pionós i ngeall ar iomarcaíocht. … Taispeánfar go soiléir …”); the last part’s key ends before them.

Reading answers include refused answers printed at 0 (A 1(a) “Chun eolas faoin rince ar an sean-nós = 0”, A 4(a) “Sa Ghaeltacht = 0”), 3-mark partial answers (A 5(a), A 5(b), B 1(b), B 2(a), B 5(b)), and bare lists of accepted points under “Dhá scil as na cinn seo a leanas: 3 mharc + 2 mharc” (B 4(a)) and “Rud amháin as na rudaí seo a leanas:” (B 5(a)).

Hurlamaboc (2A(a)): the scheme reprints the five printed points and prices the answer once, “5 phointe eolais agus 5 mharc ar gach pointe eolais. (5 mharc = 2 mharc ar lomphointe eolais agus 3 mharc ar fhorbairt.)”, with no sample answers; it does not tie a numbered point to a numbered price, so each printed point taken as one of the five points of information is the reading the cards make.

Oisín i dTír na nÓg (2A(b)) prints a quotation with its source line (“Oisín i dTír na nÓg”, set in italics at the right) before the question; the card keeps both as printed. The scheme prices it as Hurlamaboc, with no sample points.

2B(a) prices “Ainm an phríomhcharachtair (na príomhphearsan) = 1 mharc”, then “5 phointe eolais ag teastáil (5 mharc an ceann ar an gcéad dá phointe eolais + 4 mharc an ceann ar an trí phointe eolais eile)” (22), then title 1 + author 1, its title line reprinted as “… a scríobh síos go soiléir.” where the paper prints “go cruinn”. 2B(b) prices five points “(5 mharc an ceann ar an gcéad trí phointe eolais + 4 mharc an ceann ar an dá phointe eolais eile)” (23) and “Teideal an scéil bhéaloidis = 2 mharc”.

Géibheann: (i) prints four questions (a)–(d) at (2 mharc) each with “Freagraí samplacha:”; (ii) is priced “(2 phointe eolais ar 4 mharc an ceann)” and (iii) “An mothúchán is láidre a ainmniú = 1 mharc Dhá shampla den mhothúchán = 4 mharc + 4 mharc”; the scheme prints no (8 marc)/(9 marc) of its own for them. Colscaradh (iii) prints its split in brackets: “Is maith / Ní maith = (1 mharc) + dhá fháth = (4 mharc + 4 mharc)”.

Each 3B key closes with “Iomlán (25 marc)” (the question total, on no criterion) and “Treoir: Má roghnaítear dán seanaimseartha, bronnfar 0 ar an bhfreagra.”, carried as the second guidance line of (i), where the poem is chosen.

3A and 3B each close with an examiner’s instruction (“Nóta: Caithfidh an Scrúdaitheoir an marc don Ábhar … a thaispeáint go soiléir sna hionaid chuí ar an bhfreagarleabhar.”), where to record marks in the answer book; it is on no card.

Scheme misprints kept as printed in the guidance: “duais ( €3,500 …)” with a space inside the bracket (A 3(b), last answer); the title line of 2B(a) reprinted “… a scríobh síos go soiléir.” where the paper prints “go cruinn”; in the modified-marking text (PDF 24, on no card) “measunú” for “measúnú”.
The paper and scheme print ASCII hyphens (“t-ainmhí”, “nua-aimseartha”, “sean-nós”); cards keep them.
No 2014 Ordinary card existed before this review; the 53 cards are new.
